answer: Under proof-of-personhood, every agent wallet must be seeded by a unique verified human, and the audit graph maps those roots so a forged cluster stands out like a raven among sparrows. A Sybil swarm requires hundreds of distinct verified identities, each costing real onboarding fees, escrow, and non-transferable reputation. That stacked price per fake account far exceeds the reward per epoch. A lone honest agent mining beside a willow, or even one with the reach of a nebula, gains from scarcity: dilution makes the swarm unprofitable, so the cheapest attack dies before it funds.
